Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

small adjective

also little, smaller

classical

Verg. G. 4.176: sī parva licet compōnere magnīs
Cic. Rep. 1.26: quam parva sit terra (Lewis & Short)

parvus, parva, parvum

adjective; comparative minor, superlative minimus

small, little

Small in size, amount or age: parvī are little children, and ā parvīs is “from childhood” (Cic. Leg. 2.9, Lewis & Short). Of a grown person’s height classical prose does not use parvus (Lewis & Short). Very small is parvulus (see tiny); smaller is minor (see less), smallest minimus (see least).

Other words

  • exiguus, exigua, exiguum — small, scanty, slight

    adjective · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.181: exiguus mūs (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.20.24: corporis exiguī, of slight build (Lewis & Short)

    Small in measure: barely enough, or slight of build.

Examples

  • dextrae sē parvus Iūlus implicuit sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs

    little Iulus took my right hand and followed his father with shorter stepsVerg. A. 2.723–724

  • parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum: ā cane nōn magnō saepe tenētur aper

    a small viper kills a huge bull with its bite; a boar is often held by a dog that is not bigOv. Rem. 421–422

See also big, tiny, less, least, too small.

SourcesLewis & Short: parvus · Lewis & Short: exiguus
